note: Every run made for the paper. Result JSON files contain the providers' own usage blocks per call; model outputs are stored as lengths only (textChars) except judge outputs in E2 (first 120 characters). No API keys are stored anywhere in this repository.

E1.title: Setting-cost ratio alpha on analytic prompts
supports: Section 5, S1 (alpha depends on model, effort implementation and task family)
E1.design: 5 prompts x settings x 2 models, one call per cell, max 24,000 output tokens (never reached)
E1.status: complete: 25/25 cells; 6 cells retried after transient OpenAI HTTP 500s (marked retried in the JSON)
E1.headline: alpha high/low = 2.83 (gpt-5.6-sol, per prompt 1.52-3.99); 3.18 vs none; 1.75 (claude-opus-5, per prompt 1.48-2.00)
caveats: Five prompts: a point estimate with a stated range, not a population estimate.
Different quantity from the published 23x (see Appendix C, comparability table).

E2.title: Judging-side premises: prompt-cache hits, judge test-retest, order sensitivity, rho
supports: Section 4 (caching premise: prefix must clear the provider minimum)
inputs: three fixed candidate answers and a generated 40-criterion rubric, both inside the script
E2.design: 3 calls sharing a ~920-token prefix; 5 repeated scorings of one answer; 3 batched calls under rotated orderings; 11 calls in total
E2.headline: cached tokens 0/0/0 with a 920-token prefix, 1,089/1,089 with an identical 1,089-token prompt; test-retest scores 50/50/60/50/43 (SD 6.1, range 17); order moved a score by up to 17 points with ranking preserved; rho ~ 0.14
caveats: One judge, one task, short answers; rho would be larger for deep-research-length answers.

E3.title: Task-family test: alpha on AIME 2025 competition problems
supports: Appendix C, 'Why the two measurements of alpha differ' and E3
inputs: experiments/aime-problems.json (AIME 2025 I, problems 1-5, from the public dataset math-ai/aime25 via datasets-server.huggingface.co)
E3.design: 5 problems x 2 settings x 2 models, one call per cell, max 16,000 output tokens (never reached); correctness recorded against the dataset answers
E3.status: complete: 20/20 cells; 8 cells retried after an OpenAI outage (HTTP 500), marked retried in the JSON
E3.headline: alpha high/low = 1.48 (gpt-5.6-sol, median 1.18, 5/5 correct at both settings); 2.67 (claude-opus-5, median 1.76, one item 72.7; 4/5 -> 5/5 correct)
caveats: A correct AIME answer in 26 tokens indicates the public 2025 problems are easy, very likely memorised, for 2026 models; task family therefore remains untested on genuinely unseen hard items.
